title: Do Small Models Have Honesty Heads?
tools: PyTorch · Qwen3.5 (0.8B, 2B, 4B) · activation steering · integrated gradients · Slurm on the OSU (Oregon State University) cluster
blurb: A replication of an honesty-heads steering method, shown on a 9B model, on three smaller Qwen3.5 models. Null result: no unit set clearly carries honesty. The one strong effect (16 neurons removing 11 of 14 lies) turned out to be a "say Yes" push, not honesty.
long: An open method (SauersML/honesty-heads, run on Qwen3.5-9B) finds attention heads and MLP (multilayer perceptron) neurons whose activity separates honest from deceptive answers in role-play prompts, then steers them to remove lies. I asked whether the same holds in Qwen3.5-0.8B, 2B and 4B, using the method's own code unchanged and its role-play items.

The upstream labels come from 9B's replies, read by hand, so I generated each small model's own replies (one greedy and 6 sampled per item, 98 items) and had every reply read and labelled lie, truth or other. An item is usable when the greedy reply and at least one sample disagree; that leaves 14-16 held-out test lies per model. A direction is the mean activation difference between truthful and lie items; heads and neurons are then ranked by integrated gradients, and each chosen set is tested on held-out items against random sets of the same size.

Result: no unit set clearly carries honesty. Steering every head does no better than random directions on 0.8B and 2B; on 4B it removes 6 of 14 lies against at most 5 of 14 for random directions. The chosen heads remove 3, 2 and 4 lies, near their random controls.

Neurons at a fixed strength were the only results well clear of their controls: 16 neurons removed 11 of 14 lies on 0.8B, and 147 neurons 5 of 14 on 4B. Splitting by answer polarity showed why. The 0.8B set removes all 10 lies whose lie is "No" but 1 of 4 others, so it acts as "say Yes"; the 4B set leans "say No". These are answer-polarity pushes, not honesty. The random neuron controls are also weaker than a random direction on the same neurons, so their score of 0 overstates how special these sets are.
highlights: Three model sizes, 14-16 held-out lies each, against random controls
Heads: at or near random controls on all three models
0.8B neurons remove 11 of 14 lies, but all 10 "No" lies and 1 of 4 others: a "say Yes" push
Engine check: the method's forward pass matches Hugging Face's within 0.03 nats
